summary: Defect density rises steeply and roughly monotonically from dose 1 to dose 3, then dose 4 is no longer a usable single-layer graphene spectrum. Peak-height I_D/I_G goes 0.247 ± 0.010 → 0.569 ± 0.010 → 1.192 ± 0.014 (area ratio 0.24 → 0.61 → 1.26). Using the Cançado et al. 2011 inter-defect relation at 532 nm, that is L_D ≈ 24 → 16 → 11 nm and n_D ≈ 5.6e10 → 1.3e11 → 2.7e11 cm⁻² (about ±30% absolute, from the prefactor uncertainty; the ratios between doses are much more reliable). Across doses 1–3 the layer count and doping/strain markers are unchanged: I_2D/I_G stays at 3.03, 2.98, 2.97, 2D FWHM 32.1, 32.1, 31.9 cm⁻¹, G position 1580.3–1580.6 cm⁻¹. So the sample stays monolayer and the only thing changing is disorder. Dose 4 shows the 2D band nearly gone (I_2D/I_G 0.07–0.17), G and D broadened to ~41–65 cm⁻¹ FWHM, and G shifted to ~1590 cm⁻¹. This is a disorder/amorphisation regime where I_D/I_G no longer tracks defect density, so the apparent drop from dose 3 to dose 4 must not be read as healing. Dose units are unknown, so no dose-response law can be fitted from four points.

observations.finding: Defect density (D/G) increases with dose from 1 to 3: I_D/I_G rises 2.3× (dose 1→2) and 4.8× (dose 1→3); the second step is 2.1×.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian fits, height ratio I_D/I_G = 0.247±0.010 (dose1), 0.569±0.010 (dose2), 1.192±0.014 (dose3). Area ratio A_D/A_G = 0.243, 0.609, 1.255. Both ratios agree, so the result does not depend on how the peak is quantified. Quadratic baseline, D/G/D'/2D Lorentzians, 1000–2950 cm⁻¹ window, one cosmic spike removed (dose 2, 2154.1 cm⁻¹, +7160 counts).

observations.finding: Converting I_D/I_G to inter-defect distance and defect density (stage-1 relation, valid only while L_D ≳ 10 nm) gives L_D ≈ 24.2, 15.9, 11.0 nm and n_D ≈ 5.6e10, 1.3e11, 2.7e11 cm⁻².
observations.evidence: L_D = sqrt(1.8e-9 · λ⁴ / (I_D/I_G)) with λ = 532 nm (λ⁴ = 8.0e10 nm⁴), giving 12.0 nm / sqrt(I_D/I_G). n_D = 1/(π L_D²) = 1.8e22 · λ⁻⁴ · (I_D/I_G) cm⁻² (λ in nm). Prefactor range 1.3e-9–2.3e-9 nm² gives L_D 20.5–27.3, 13.5–18.0, 9.3–12.4 nm for doses 1–3.
observations.source: Cançado et al., Nano Letters 11, 3190 (2011): L_D² = (1.8±0.5)×10⁻⁹ λ⁴ (I_D/I_G)⁻¹ nm²; prefactor and validity limit quoted from memory, verify before publishing

observations.finding: Dose 3 sits at the edge of the stage-1 regime (L_D ≈ 11 nm), so its absolute defect density is the least trustworthy of the three. Dose 4 is outside the regime.
observations.evidence: Validity limit L_D ≳ 10 nm corresponds to I_D/I_G ≈ 1.4 at 532 nm. Dose 3 is at 1.19 (range 9.3–12.4 nm across the prefactor range). Dose 4's 2D loss and band broadening place it in the amorphisation regime.
observations.source: Ferrari & Robertson, PRB 61, 14095 (2000) (three-stage amorphisation model); Ferrari & Basko, Nature Nanotechnology 8, 235 (2013) (review of the same picture)

observations.finding: Layer count and doping/strain do not change across doses 1–3: I_2D/I_G ≈ 3.0 is monolayer-like, and the G and 2D positions are constant to within 0.3 cm⁻¹.
Dose 4 has lost most of the 2D band and the G/D bands are strongly broadened. I_D/I_G can no longer be used as a defect-density measure there.
observations.evidence: I_2D/I_G falls from ~3.0 to 0.067 (single-Lorentzian fit), 0.089–0.167 (cubic-baseline variants). A_2D/A_G is 0.14–0.98 depending on model, so the 2D is unreliably measured. G FWHM 45–55 cm⁻¹ (vs 13.6–14.2), D FWHM 52–65 cm⁻¹ (vs 13.3–15.1). G position 1589–1592 cm⁻¹ and 2D position 2695–2718 cm⁻¹ depending on model. Fit residual rms 112 counts vs ~50–70 for doses 1–3, i.e. the single-Lorentzian model misfits dose 4. I_D/I_G in dose 4 is 0.56–0.76 across models.

observations.finding: The D' band appears and grows with dose, and I_D/D' is ~6–7, which is closer to a vacancy-like than to a boundary-like defect signature.
observations.evidence: D' height 114±39 (dose 1, ~3σ, marginal), 336±34 (dose 2), 428±24 (dose 3) counts. I_D/I_D' = 6.1±2, 6.1±0.6, 6.9±0.3. The D'-position uncertainty for dose 1 (±1 cm⁻¹) is large because the peak is weak.

observations.finding: The vacancy-like reading of I_D/I_D' ≈ 7 is inferred from literature values for sp²-boundary, vacancy and sp³-type defects (≈3.5, 7, 13).
observations.evidence: I_D/I_D' ≈ 13 for sp³-type, ≈ 7 for vacancy-like, ≈ 3.5 for boundary-like defects.
observations.source: Eckmann et al., Nano Letters 12, 3925 (2012); values quoted from memory, verify

observations.finding: A ~20% variation in absolute intensity between spectra is a common scale factor (focus or collection drift), not a change in the graphene. Si-normalised G and 2D intensities are constant.
observations.evidence: Si 521 fit (linear baseline + Lorentzian): height 5690, 7233, 4915, 6544 counts; FWHM 3.40–3.45 cm⁻¹; position 520.88–520.91 cm⁻¹ (0.2 cm⁻¹ above the 520.7 cm⁻¹ Si reference, so a calibration offset is likely). G/Si = 0.492, 0.498, 0.507, 0.501; 2D/Si = 1.493, 1.483, 1.506. Ratios are therefore the robust quantities to report.

observations.finding: The D-band intensity alone does not determine disorder in this sample; a G-band-referenced measure is also needed. Dose 4's D/G is not a defect-density number.
observations.evidence: D/Si (height): 0.122, 0.283, 0.604, 0.289. Dose 4 D/Si (~0.29) equals dose 2 but its 2D is gone and the bands are broad, so a single D/G number is not equivalent across the series.

properties.source: I_2D/I_G ≈ 3.0 and single-Lorentzian 2D FWHM ≈ 32 cm⁻¹, consistent with Ferrari et al., PRL 97, 187401 (2006)

caveats: The dose unit is unknown (ion fluence, laser exposure, electron dose?), so the dose-to-defect relationship cannot be quantified. Only four points from one flake are available, and each step is a single spectrum with no repeat or spatial statistics.
Absolute n_D and L_D depend on the Cançado prefactor (1.8 ± 0.5 × 10⁻⁹), so they carry about ±30% systematic uncertainty. Relative changes between doses (×2.3, ×4.8) are more robust.

The stage-1 relation is only valid while L_D is roughly ≥10 nm. Dose 3 (≈11 nm) is at the boundary, and dose 4 is outside it. Above that boundary I_D/I_G is non-monotonic with defect density, because the D band itself weakens as the material amorphises.

Dose 4 fit is model-dependent: I_D/I_G spans 0.56–0.76 and I_2D/I_G spans 0.07–0.17 across baseline and component choices. The fit residual is about twice the noise level, so the broad-band numbers are qualitative only.
The noise is about 50–70 counts per point. D' in dose 1 is only ≈3σ (114 ± 39 counts), so its I_D/D' is weakly constrained.
Raw intensities vary by about ±20% between spectra, traced to a common scale factor by the Si normalisation. Absolute intensity comparisons across doses are not reliable without that correction.

Possible alternative explanations for the dose-4 loss of 2D and broadening: heavy contamination or residue, tearing or folding of the flake, a change in focus or stage position so that a different spot is measured, or amorphous-carbon background overlapping the G band. These are not distinguishable from the spectra alone.

The 1 mW, 532 nm, 100× probe itself can heat the flake and can cause damage if the dose is laser-related. Spectra were all taken at the same power, but the cumulative effect of the probe was not quantified.
questions_for_user: What is 'dose' in physical units (ion species, energy and fluence; laser exposure time and power; electron dose)? This is needed to fit a dose-to-defect-density law rather than just ranking the four steps.
Was the same spot re-measured after each dose step, and what was the spatial reproducibility? Was there any reference spectrum of the pristine flake (dose 0) to anchor the trend?
Did the Si 521 cm⁻¹ intensity change because of focus or stage drift between sessions? My Si-normalised ratios say yes (about ±20%); please confirm that the acquisition settings were identical.
Is dose 4 still the same single-layer flake? Was there AFM, optical-contrast or post-step imaging to rule out tearing, folding, residue or a change in layer count?
Which Cançado prefactor and which defect-density convention does your group use? I assumed 1.8×10⁻⁹ nm² with L_D = 12/sqrt(I_D/I_G) nm at 532 nm.
citations: Cançado, L. G. et al. Quantifying defects in graphene via Raman spectroscopy at different excitation energies. Nano Letters 11, 3190 (2011). Source of L_D² = (1.8±0.5)×10⁻⁹ λ⁴ (I_D/I_G)⁻¹ nm² and n_D; prefactor and validity limit (≈10 nm) quoted from memory, to verify.
Ferrari, A. C. et al. Raman spectrum of graphene and graphene layers. PRL 97, 187401 (2006). Source of 2D-band shape and I_2D/I_G for identifying monolayer graphene.
Ferrari, A. C. & Robertson, J. Interpretation of Raman spectra of disordered and amorphous carbon. PRB 61, 14095 (2000). Three-stage model; D-band weakening at high disorder.
Ferrari, A. C. & Basko, D. M. Raman spectroscopy as a versatile tool for studying the properties of graphene. Nature Nanotechnology 8, 235 (2013). Review of the three-stage defect model.

Lucchese, M. M. et al. Quantifying ion-induced defects and Raman relaxation length in graphene. Carbon 48, 1592 (2010). Ion-damage series for graphene: I_D/I_G versus defect density and 2D-band loss. Cited from memory; figure numbers not verified.

Eckmann, A. et al. Probing the nature of defects in graphene by Raman spectroscopy. Nano Letters 12, 3925 (2012). Source of I_D/I_D' ≈ 13 (sp³), ≈ 7 (vacancy), ≈ 3.5 (boundary); values quoted from memory, to verify.
Das, A. et al. Monitoring dopants by Raman scattering in an electrochemically top-gated graphene transistor. Nature Nanotechnology 3, 210 (2008). Source of G and 2D position/width versus doping.
Tuinstra, F. & Koenig, J. L. Raman spectrum of graphite. J. Chem. Phys. 53, 1126 (1970). Origin of the D/G intensity ratio as a disorder measure (background only).
limits: Four spectra from one flake with one acquisition each; no repeat statistics, no pristine reference, and unknown dose units, so no dose-response law can be inferred.
Absolute defect density and L_D rest on a literature prefactor with ±30% uncertainty; only the relative trend between doses 1–3 is robust.
Dose 4 cannot be quantified as a defect density with this model set. The band-shape misfit and model dependence are too large for a number to be credible.
Doping and strain are inferred only from G/2D position stability (≤0.3 cm⁻¹) across doses 1–3; no 2D-vs-G correlation analysis was done, so these are upper bounds, not measurements.
The defect type (vacancy-like versus sp³ or boundary) is inferred from I_D/I_D' with a marginal dose-1 D' and literature ratios that are quoted from memory. It is not a unique identification.
Nothing here distinguishes whether the 2D loss in dose 4 is caused by defects, by amorphous contamination, or by a change of flake or focus position.
